title: card-sort-plan template variables
description: Values for templates/card-sort-plan.md.j2 and templates/card-sort-plan.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from card-sort-plan.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

card_count.title: Card count
card_count.description: How many cards, 30 to 60. Fewer than 30 rarely shows structure; more than 60 and participants fatigue and start sorting by first letter, which looks like a real finding.

category_1.title: Category 1
category_1.description: The category 1 used under 'Categories (Closed Sort Only)'.

category_2.title: Category 2
category_2.description: The category 2 used under 'Categories (Closed Sort Only)'.

date.title: Date
date.description: The date used under 'Card Sort Plan'.

objective_one.title: Objective one
objective_one.description: The first question this answers, phrased so the result could contradict your current navigation. "Do users group billing with account or with reports?" - not "is our IA intuitive?"

participant_count.title: Participant count
participant_count.description: How many participants. Roughly 15-20 for an open sort, 30 or more for a closed one. Under that the co-occurrence percentages below are not stable enough to draw a boundary with.

project_name.description: The site, app or section whose information architecture is being tested. One IA per study - sorting cards from two different products produces clusters that describe neither.

researcher.title: Researcher
researcher.description: Who runs the study and writes the labels. Card wording is the single biggest source of bias here, so the author of the cards should be on the record.

sort_type.title: Sort type
sort_type.description: Open discovers the users' own groupings and their names for them; closed tests an IA you already have. Running closed first is how you validate a structure you never questioned.

tool.title: Tool
tool.description: The tool or physical setup used. It decides what analysis you get - some export a co-occurrence matrix, some only a dendrogram, and the analysis plan below assumes the matrix.
